sections.content: How many people are "local government administrative occupations"?

72,630 people

were counted on the census as "local government administrative occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Local government administrative occupations undertake a variety of administrative and clerical duties in local government offices and departments.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "local government administrative occupations" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "local government administrative occupations", 16.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "local government administrative occupations" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "local government administrative occupations" included:

  • print finishing and binding workers
  • electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers
  • window cleaners

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "local government administrative occupations" there were more women than men (71.2% compared with 28.8%).

This means "local government administrative occupations" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 28.8% and women made up 71.2% of "local government administrative occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "local government administrative occupations" included:

  • officers of non-governmental organisations
  • financial administrative occupations (other)
  • waiters and waitresses

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "local government administrative occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "local government administrative occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "local government administrative occupations", 14.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (69.3% compared with 30.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.7%) than self-employed (1.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included County Durham, this is in the region of the North East.
